record.original_question: Let E be a set of homogeneous linear equations which is partition regular; that is, E has a non-trivial monochromatic solution for any r-coloring of Z. For positive integer N and r, what is the minimum number fE(N; r) of monochromatic solutions to E which can occur for an r-coloring of [1; N]? It follows from general results of Frankl, Graham, and Rodl that a positive fraction (depending only on E and r) of all solutions are monochromatic. However, it seems to be di cult to determine exactly the best possible constant. It is known that if r = 2 and E consists of a single equation x + y = z, then fE(N; r) = N 2(1 + o(1))=22 (Robertson-Zeilberger , Schoen ). artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a finite set E of homogeneous linear equations in integer variables partition regular if, for every positive integer r and every r-coloring of the positive integers, the system E has a non-trivial monochromatic solution (one in which not all variables are equal). For positive integers N and r, let f_E(N;r) denote the minimum, over all r-colorings of {1,2,...,N}, of the number of non-trivial monochromatic solutions of E with all coordinates in {1,2,...,N}.

Take r = 2 and let E consist of the single equation x + y = 2z (so monochromatic solutions correspond to monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions, including those with x = y = z when counted as trivial, which are excluded). Determine the limiting constant
   c = lim_{N → ∞} f_E(N;2) / N^2,
or equivalently determine the asymptotic value of f_E(N;2) up to a factor 1 + o(1).

It is known that this constant satisfies the bounds 1/21.67... ≤ c ≤ 117/2192 = 1/18.735..., while a uniformly random 2-coloring achieves 1/16. The problem asks for the exact value of c (in particular, whether c = 117/2192).
artifact.status_search_result: The exact asymptotic constant for the minimum number of monochromatic 3-term APs in a 2-coloring of [1,N] remains open. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:2301.00336, 2023) has improved the lower bound and connected the problem to a continuous analogue on [0,1], proving the Parrilo–Robertson–Saracino conjectured coloring is optimal among certain restricted (anti-symmetric, ≤12 block) colorings, but the gap between the lower bound (~1/21.67) and the upper bound 117/2192 has not been closed.

status_evidence.title: From discrete to continuous: Monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: 1675/32768 · n²(1+o(1)) ≤ V(n) ≤ 117/2192 · n²(1+o(1)); the PRS conjectured coloring is optimal among anti-symmetric colorings with ≤12 blocks.
status_evidence.claim: The exact constant remains unknown; current best bounds still leave a gap, and only restricted optimality of the conjectured extremal coloring is known.

status_evidence.claim: The problem of determining the exact asymptotic constant is studied but not resolved.
